newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart Stores segments gain, int'l profits.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart Stores segments gain, int'l profits.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc, which reported record sales of $25 billion in the first quarter, said on Monday that its Wal-Mart and Sam's Club units both reported higher operating profits and its international unit posted a profit.
Wal-Mart's international division had an operating profit of $6 million for the quarter, compared with an operating loss of $16 million for the same period last year.
Wal-Mart's Supercenters, which include grocery stores, helped with Wal-Mart division post operating profits of $1.26 billion, compared with $1.12 billion in last year's first quarter.
The Sam's Club division had operating profit for the quarter of $189 million, an increase of 5 percent compared to $180 million for the previous year, Wal-Mart said.

David Glass, Wal-Mart's president and chief executive officer, said in a statement, "Highlights include our international division posting an operating profit in the traditionally difficult first quarter, continued Supercenter growth, and our ongoing improvements in asset management and cash flow."
Glass cited the company's $2 billion stock repurchase program and operating improvements as factors in the improved first quarter earnings.
During the quarter, Wal-Mart opened two discount stores; 18 Supercenters, including 17 replacements of discount stores; three international units in Mexico; and two Sam's Clubs.

As of April 30, 1997, Wal-Mart had 1,945 Wal-Mart stores, 362 Supercenters, 438 Sam's Clubs, 6 Argentina units, 5 Brazilian units, 136 Canadian Wal-Mart stores, 2 China stores, 2 Indonesian Supercenters, 153 Mexican units, and 11 Puerto Rico units.
